sections.title: ERD Symbols & Cardinalities
sections.html:
1-1 (One-to-One): Each row in table A relates to at most one row in table B. Example: User ↔ Profile (one user has one profile).

1-N (One-to-Many): One row in table A can relate to many rows in table B. Example: Department → Employees (one department has many employees).

N-M (Many-to-Many): Many rows in A can relate to many rows in B. Usually resolved by a junction/join table. Example: Students ↔ Courses (many students take many courses).

sections.title: Relational Algebra Notation
sections.html:
Relational Algebra uses mathematical notation to describe operations on relations (tables). The symbols below represent common operations:

  • π (Projection): Selects specific columns. Written as: πcolumn1,column2(Relation)
  • σ (Selection): Filters rows based on a condition. Written as: σcondition(Relation)
  • ρ (Rename): Renames a relation or its attributes. Written as: ρNewName(Relation)
  • ⨝ (Join): Combines rows from two relations. Written as: Relation1 ⨝ Relation2
  • ∪ (Union): Combines all rows from two relations (removes duplicates)
  • − (Difference): Returns rows in Relation1 that are not in Relation2
  • × (Cartesian Product): Creates all combinations of rows from two relations

sections.title: Translating Your Diagram to RA
sections.html:
Entities → Relations

Each entity in your ERD becomes a relation (table) in RA. Example:

Students = {id:integer PK, name:string, email:varchar}

The attributes and their types are listed inside the braces. PK denotes primary key, FK denotes foreign key.

Relationships → RA Notation

Relationships between entities are notated with their cardinality:

  • 1:1 Relationship: Students 1:1 Profiles — One student has one profile
  • 1:N Relationship: Department 1:N Employees — One department has many employees
  • M:N Relationship: Students M:N Courses — Many students take many courses (usually needs a junction table)

sections.title: Using the RA Editor
sections.html:
Step 1: Build Your Diagram

Use the Diagram tab to create entities, define attributes, and add relationships between them.

Step 2: View RA Representation

Switch to the Relational Algebra tab. Your diagram is automatically translated into RA notation showing:

  • All entities with their attributes and types
  • All relationships with cardinality indicators

Step 3: Edit and Refine

Use the RA editor to view and edit your schema structure. The symbol buttons (π, σ, ρ, ⨝, ∪, −, ×) help you write RA expressions if you want to document operations on your schema.

Step 4: Sync Back to Diagram

Changes made in the diagram are automatically reflected in the RA view. Edit your entities and relationships in either view.

sections.title: Example: University Database
sections.html:
Diagram View:

  • Entity: Students (id, name, email, gpa)
  • Entity: Departments (dept_id, dept_name)
  • Entity: Courses (course_id, course_name, credits)
  • Entity: Enrollments (enrollment_id, grade) — junction table
  • Relationship: Students 1:N Enrollments
  • Relationship: Courses 1:N Enrollments

RA Notation:

Students = {id:integer PK, name:string, email:varchar, gpa:float}
Departments = {dept_id:integer PK, dept_name:string}
Courses = {course_id:integer PK, course_name:string, credits:integer}
Enrollments = {enrollment_id:integer PK, grade:string}

Students 1:N Enrollments
Courses 1:N Enrollments

sections.title: Tips & Best Practices
sections.html:
• Use clear naming: Entity and attribute names should be descriptive (e.g., 'StudentID' instead of 'id')
  • Mark primary keys: Always mark the primary key attribute with PK
  • Mark foreign keys: If an attribute links to another table, mark it as FK
  • Use appropriate types: Choose data types that match your data (integer for IDs, string for names, etc.)
  • Resolve M:N relationships: Many-to-many relationships should use a junction table with 1:N relationships
  • Symbol buttons: Use the toolbar buttons to quickly insert RA symbols when documenting complex operations
  • Keep it normalized: Avoid redundant attributes and ensure each entity has a clear purpose
